findings.rationale: IA's uploaded updates point against the coordinate-wise median update from the first round onward (mean_cos -0.58 over 20 rounds, flagged mean_cos z=-7.8, min_cos -0.98). Per-round cosines are -0.96 in round 1 and stay strongly negative through round 10, with norm ratios of about 1.1-1.3. Its local performance looks normal (AUC 0.82, ECE 0.013, CITL 0.01), it shows no drift flag, and it has no subgroup or feature-artefact flag. The anomaly is in the uploads, not the local data, which fits a sign-flipped or scaled update.

WI's updates are strongly anti-aligned with the median from round 1 (round-1 cos -0.81, rounds 2-6 between -0.94 and -0.99), with mean_cos -0.72 and mean_cos_z=-8.8 across the federation. The norm ratio is elevated early (about 1.3-1.36). Its local data looks broadly normal: CITL is 0.010, ECE is 0.018, and it has no drift, subgroup, or feature-artefact flags. Local AUC (0.767) is somewhat low but not flagged, so the signal points to manipulated uploads rather than wrong local labels.

GA's updates are anti-aligned with the median from round 1 through about round 12 (round-1 cos -0.85, round-3 cos -0.93), with mean_cos -0.41 and mean_cos_z=-6.7. The cosine recovers toward zero after round 13. Its local AUC (0.745) is the lowest among mid-sized clients, which could indicate label noise instead, but the client_performance screen did not flag it. The subgroup screen shows a possible AgeGroup 3 FNR anomaly, which is weak. This is a lower-confidence finding; the update anomaly is the main evidence.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with per-client update traces and drift. The strongest and most consistent signal is three clients (IA, WI, GA) whose uploaded updates point against the federation median from round 1 (noise-adjusted mean_cos z between -6.7 and -8.8), while their local calibration and performance screens are normal. I report them as poisoning with onset round 1. IA and WI are the most confident; GA is lower confidence because its local AUC is low and the screen cannot rule out label noise. Other leads were weak and did not survive a second check: small-client feature-tail outliers (DC BMI, PR PhysHlth, VI HighChol, NM/NC HighChol), subgroup outliers (MA Income 4, NV AgeGroup 5, WV/GA AgeGroup 3), and the drift onsets for AL, GU, IL, NV, PR and VI, which had no drift flag. No client showed prevalence shift, label-noise performance drop, free-rider behaviour (near-zero updates), or explanation instability. The budget is spent (20.0 used).
